The emperor of Japan from 1867 until his death in 1912, whose personal name was Mutsuhito. In his name Japan ended samurai rule, built modern industry and an army, and became a world power. His reign, the Meiji era, gave its name to the whole transformation.

He came to the throne at fourteen, as the Tokugawa shogunate was collapsing after Perry's ships forced Japan open. In 1868 the Meiji Restoration returned power to the throne, and the court moved from Kyoto to Edo, renamed Tokyo.

The changes made in his name:

  • The domains were abolished in 1871 and the samurai class ended.
  • Schooling for all began in 1872, and conscription built a national army.
  • Railways, such as the Tokyo to Yokohama line of 1872, factories and banks were built with Western help.
  • The Meiji Constitution of 1889 made him sovereign, with an elected Diet.

How much he decided himself is debated. Most policy came from a small group of oligarchs who had led the restoration, and he served mainly as the symbol that united the country. He was presented as a modern monarch in Western uniform.

By his death, Japan had beaten China in 1895 and Russia in 1905, the first Asian victory over a European power in modern times. It had annexed Korea in 1910 and ended the unequal treaties. One of his generals, Nogi Maresuke, killed himself on the day of his funeral. His grandson was Hirohito.
